content: The co-administration of medications that induce fluid and electrolyte abnormalities with sodium sulfate, potassium sulfate, and magnesium sulfate can significantly increase the risk of adverse events such as seizures, arrhythmias, and renal impairment. Close monitoring is required in these scenarios. 1. Sodium sulfate/potassium sulfate/magnesium sulfate and Irbesartan: The combination increases the toxicity of irbesartan. Monitor closely for signs of toxicity. 2. Sodium sulfate/potassium sulfate/magnesium sulfate and Iron Dextran Complex: This combination decreases the levels of iron dextran complex due to inhibition of gastrointestinal absorption. This applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Administer iron products at least 2 hours before or no less than 6 hours after each dose to avoid chelation with magnesium. 3. Sodium sulfate/potassium sulfate/magnesium sulfate and Iron Sucrose: Similar to iron dextran, this combination decreases iron sucrose levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. Administer iron products at least 2 hours before or no less than 6 hours after each dose. 4. Sodium sulfate/potassium sulfate/magnesium sulfate and Isoniazid: The combination increases the toxicity of isoniazid. Monitor closely for adverse effects. 5. Sodium sulfate/potassium sulfate/magnesium sulfate and Calcium Channel Blockers (e.g., Isradipine, Nicardipine, Nifedipine, Nimodipine, Nisoldipine): These combinations may increase the effects of either agent through an unknown mechanism. Monitor for hypotension or muscle weakness, especially in patients with elevated serum magnesium concentrations. 6. Sodium sulfate/potassium sulfate/magnesium sulfate and Ivosidenib: This combination increases the toxicity of ivosidenib by prolonging the QTc interval. Consider pre-dose and post-colonoscopy ECGs in patients at increased risk of serious cardiac arrhythmias. 7. Sodium sulfate/potassium sulfate/magnesium sulfate and Kanamycin: The combination increases the toxicity of kanamycin. Monitor closely for adverse effects. 8. Sodium sulfate/potassium sulfate/magnesium sulfate and Ketoconazole: The combination increases the toxicity of ketoconazole. Monitor closely for adverse effects. 9. Sodium sulfate/potassium sulfate/magnesium sulfate and Ketoprofen: The combination increases the toxicity of ketoprofen. Monitor closely for adverse effects. 10. Sodium sulfate/potassium sulfate/magnesium sulfate and Ketorolac (including intranasal): The combination increases the toxicity of ketorolac. Monitor closely for adverse effects. 11. Sodium sulfate/potassium sulfate/magnesium sulfate and Lanthanum Carbonate: The combination increases the toxicity of lanthanum carbonate. Monitor closely for adverse effects. 12. Sodium sulfate/potassium sulfate/magnesium sulfate and Lefamulin: This combination increases the toxicity of lefamulin by prolonging the QTc interval. Consider pre-dose and post-colonoscopy ECGs in patients at increased risk of serious cardiac arrhythmias. 13. Sodium sulfate/potassium sulfate/magnesium sulfate and Lenvatinib: The combination increases the toxicity of lenvatinib by prolonging the QTc interval. Consider pre-dose and post-colonoscopy ECGs in patients at increased risk of serious cardiac arrhythmias. 14. Sodium sulfate/potassium sulfate/magnesium sulfate and Levofloxacin: This combination decreases the levels of levofloxacin due to inhibition of gastrointestinal absorption. Administer fluoroquinolones at least 2 hours before or no less than 6 hours after each dose to avoid chelation with magnesium. 15. Sodium sulfate/potassium sulfate/magnesium sulfate and Levothyroxine: This combination decreases the levels of levothyroxine due to inhibition of gastrointestinal absorption. Administer levothyroxine at least 4 hours after each dose to avoid chelation with magnesium. 16. Sodium sulfate/potassium sulfate/magnesium sulfate and Lisinopril: The combination increases the toxicity of lisinopril. Monitor closely for adverse effects. 17. Sodium sulfate/potassium sulfate/magnesium sulfate and Lopinavir: This combination increases the toxicity of lopinavir by prolonging the QTc interval. Consider pre-dose and post-colonoscopy ECGs in patients at increased risk of serious cardiac arrhythmias. 18. Sodium sulfate/potassium sulfate/magnesium sulfate and Losartan: The combination increases the toxicity of losartan. Monitor closely for adverse effects. 19. Sodium sulfate/potassium sulfate/magnesium sulfate and Loxapine (including inhaled): The combination increases the effects of loxapine through an unknown mechanism. Monitor for enhanced CNS depression, especially when using higher doses of magnesium sulfate with a CNS depressant. 20. Sodium sulfate/potassium sulfate/magnesium sulfate and Lurasidone: The combination increases the effects of lurasidone through an unknown mechanism. Monitor for enhanced CNS depression, especially when using higher doses of magnesium sulfate with a CNS depressant. 21. Sodium sulfate/potassium sulfate/magnesium sulfate and Macimorelin: This combination increases the toxicity of macimorelin by prolonging the QTc interval. Consider pre-dose and post-colonoscopy ECGs in patients at increased risk of serious cardiac arrhythmias. 22. Consider pre-dose and post-colonoscopy ECGs in patients at increased risk of serious cardiac arrhythmias. 29. Sodium sulfate/potassium sulfate/magnesium sulfate and Methyclothiazide: The combination increases the toxicity of methyclothiazide. Monitor closely for adverse effects. 30. Sodium sulfate/potassium sulfate/magnesium sulfate and Methylprednisolone: The combination increases the toxicity of methylprednisolone. Monitor closely for adverse effects. 31. Sodium sulfate/potassium sulfate/magnesium sulfate and Minocycline: This combination decreases the levels of minocycline due to inhibition of gastrointestinal absorption. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Administer tetracyclines at least 2 hours before or no less than 6 hours after each dose to avoid chelation with magnesium. 32. Monitor for enhanced CNS depression, especially when using higher doses of magnesium sulfate with a CNS depressant. 34. Administer fluoroquinolones at least 2 hours before or no less than 6 hours after each dose to avoid chelation with magnesium. 36. Consider pre-dose and post-colonoscopy ECGs in patients at increased risk of serious cardiac arrhythmias. 40. Sodium sulfate/potassium sulfate/magnesium sulfate and Norfloxacin: This combination decreases the levels of norfloxacin due to inhibition of gastrointestinal absorption. Administer fluoroquinolones at least 2 hours before or no less than 6 hours after each dose to avoid chelation with magnesium.
